questions.question: What condition must the indices meet to be on the main diagonal of a square matrix?
explanations: That is the condition of the secondary or anti-diagonal.
Correct. On the main diagonal, the row index equals the column index.
row * col == 0 corresponds to the first row or the first column.
row != col are the elements outside the main diagonal.

questions.question: What allows matrices in Java to have rows of different lengths?
options: That they are arrays of arrays
Java does not allow jagged rows
explanations: Inheritance is not related to array structure.
Correct. Each row is an independent array, so they can have different lengths.
The garbage collector frees memory; it does not affect array structure.
Java does allow jagged rows (ragged arrays).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element matriz[i][j]?
explanations: It does not require traversing elements; access is direct by index.
Correct. As with 1D arrays, index-based access to any element is O(1).
It does not require traversing all the elements.
It does not use binary search or a tree structure.

options: int[][] m = new int[3][]; m[0]=new int[2]; m[1]=new int[4]; m[2]=new int[3]
explanations: That syntax is not valid for jagged matrices.
Correct. The rows are declared without specifying columns, then each row is assigned individually.
The declaration syntax is incorrect.
